Homicide/violent crime reduction (source 3) (e.g. DALYs)
rows.explainer: Two RCTs were conducted in Chicago and tested a program called Becoming a Man (BAM), developed by the nonprofit Youth Guidance for economically disadvantaged youths. Participation in the program reduced total arrests during the intervention by 28-35%, and reduced violent crime arrests by 45-50%. It also improved school engagement, and in follow up data increased graduation rates by 12-19% (Heller et al. 2017). https://academic.oup.com/qje/article-abstract/132/1/1/2724542?redirectedFrom=fulltext

rows.label: Homicide/violent crime reduction (source 6)
rows.explainer: An RCT of the Rapid Employment and Development Initiative (READI) Chicago tested in a cohort of 2,456 men at high risk for gun violence, whether CBT and 18-month job program would reduce gun violence. After 20 months, there was no statistically significant change in the combined index of three serious violence measures, the study's main outcome. However, the program shows potential, as one of the measures, shooting and homicide arrests, decreased by 65% (p = 0.13 after adjusting for multiple testing). In a pre-specified group, of participants referred by outreach workers, the decline in arrests and victimizations of shootings and homicides were down 79% and 43% respectively. This was statistically significant even after multiple-testing adjustments https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/139/1/1/7220727

rows.explainer:
Method 1: "The “chronic offenders” at age 32 were defined as the 24 men (6% of the sample) who committed half of all officially recorded offenses (Farrington & West, 1993)." https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/0-306-47945-1_5 Only 40% of men are offenders (164 males). So they commit the remaining half of the offenses. That means the chronic offenders commit 3.42 times more crime than the average (see calculation https://chatgpt.com/share/42f324d7-ce24-4945-bac4-6d589c5e375b)
Method 2: This is assuming the charity would target offenders who are more likely to commit crimes than the average offender in the country. This could easily be 5x if we consider the pareto principle of 20% of offenders commit 80% of crimes.
Went with method 1 https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/0-306-47945-1_5

summary: Ambitious Impact's 2024 estimate (2025 idea report) for a new charity delivering cognitive behavioural therapy to people who have offended or are at high risk of offending, to reduce crime (modelled for Brazil). The idea ACTRA was founded to run. Its bottom line is the cost per DALY-equivalent averted, adjusted for targeting; AIM counts victims' economic losses in it at 0.43 DALYs per year of doubled consumption (1/2.3, GiveWell's rate; 'Main CEA'!B54).
